title: Best Product Photographers (2026): How to Hire One Online
description: How to hire a product photographer online: what the package should include, how to ship and brief, what drives the price and red flags.
intro: Online shoppers cannot touch your product, so the photos do the selling. Good product photos show the item accurately, in the sizes and backgrounds each store requires. Remote shoots go wrong when products are damaged in shipping, colors are edited away from reality, or the shot list was never agreed. This guide covers how to avoid that.

faq.q: How does remote product photography work?
faq.a: You ship the products to the photographer, they shoot them in their studio, edit the images and send the files. Agree on return shipping, or whether the products are kept or disposed of, before sending anything.

faq.q: What is the difference between white-background and lifestyle photos?
faq.a: White-background photos show the product alone, which many marketplaces require for the main image. Lifestyle photos show it in use or in a setting, which helps buyers imagine owning it. Most listings benefit from both.

faq.q: Which image sizes do I need?
faq.a: Check each sales channel's requirements, such as minimum pixel size, background and aspect ratio. Give the list to the photographer so the images can be exported correctly.

faq.q: Can the photos be edited heavily?
faq.a: Cleaning dust and adjusting light is normal. Changing the color, shape or size of the product misleads buyers and leads to returns. Ask for accurate colors.
Confirm your usage rights in writing: on which channels, in ads, and for how long. Some photographers license images rather than transfer full rights.
